text:
I did not sleep that morning. I sat at my kitchen table in the gray light, with the phone propped against the sugar bowl, and played the recordings over and over.

The hall light bothered me, but something else bothered me more, and I could not say exactly what it was. It sat at the back of my mind like a word I could not remember.

Then I saw it. I had been studying the picture instead of the numbers in the corner, where every recording carries a small white date stamp. I scrolled back through all nine nights, one by one, and the dates were wrong. The first recording, the one I watched during my break, carried a stamp one day ahead of the day I actually watched it. Every recording after it did exactly the same.

I checked the calendar on my telephone, I checked the settings in the application, and I even restarted the camera and set the clock by hand. The recordings kept arriving, and the stamps kept saying tomorrow.

I am a nurse, and when a number looks wrong, I test the equipment. So I tore a page from the notepad by the refrigerator and wrote a message in thick black marker. If you can read this, tell me. I taped it to the outside of the front door at eye level and went to work with my heart ticking like a clock.

All night I tried to imagine other explanations, like a stolen password, a faulty update, or a clever prankster with a computer program. None of them explained the footprints.

At 3:12 the phone chimed in my pocket, so I stepped into the stairwell, where nobody could see my face, and opened the recording.

The date stamp read tomorrow. The hooded figure stood on my porch, still as stone, and on the door in front of it hung my note. Beneath my question, in black marker, someone had written an answer in my own handwriting.
summary: She sees that every recording is date-stamped for tomorrow, tests it by taping a note to her door, and the next recording shows an answer in her own handwriting.
